defect.summary: WebSocket endpoint has no authentication and no Origin validation, enabling cross-origin hijacking of a localhost agent that can execute shell commands.
defect.detail: The `WebSocketServer` is created without `verifyClient` and the `connection` handler accepts any socket, so a malicious web page the user visits can open `ws://127.0.0.1:18888/ws` (browsers do not apply same-origin policy to WebSockets, and 18888 is the hard-coded default port in address.ts). Once connected, that page can send `user_message` to start agent runs and reply `permission_response: "allow"` to its own `permission_request` broadcasts, approving Bash/PowerShell execution and yielding remote code execution as the user. Standard mitigation (rejecting connections whose `Origin` header is not the served host, or requiring a shared token) is absent. Review 2026-09-30: still no verifyClient/Origin/token validation anywhere in server.ts; parseRemoteAddress additionally permits binding any interface (e.g. 0.0.0.0), widening exposure beyond loopback when chosen.

defect.summary: tmux spawn embeds the shell-quoted command inside outer double quotes, re-activating $, backticks, " and \ in LLM-provided task text
defect.detail: spawnTeammate builds `tmux new-session ... "${cmd}"` where cmd's tokens were single-quoted by shellQuote. Inside the outer double quotes those single quotes are literal, so a task string containing `$(...)`, backticks, or `"` is interpreted by the leader's own shell during execSync — e.g. task text `x"; rm -rf ~; "` breaks out of the quoting entirely. The shellQuote JSDoc documents this caveat but the exposure remains: task text originates from model output and can execute arbitrary commands in the leader process. Review 2026-09-30: teammate name IS validated (teams/protocol.ts:43 /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/, tools.ts:153) but task text is not sanitized (teams/index.ts:355); the tmux branch embeds shellQuote output inside outer double quotes where $, backtick, " and \ stay shell-active. The iTerm branch is NOT affected: its single-quoted tokens reach the tab shell verbatim (no outer double-quote layer).

defect.summary: Mutating team tools declare category "read", which the permission checker auto-allows without prompting
defect.detail: TeamCreateTool, SpawnTeammateTool, SendMessageTool, and TeamDeleteTool all set `category = "read"` (tools.ts:52, 108, 186, 407). PermissionChecker.modeDecide returns "allow" for category "read" in default and plan modes, so TeamDelete — which stops running members and recursively deletes the team directory — and process-spawning tools execute with no permission prompt. Comparable mutating tools (TaskStop, TaskCreate, TaskUpdate) correctly use "command".

defect.summary: InstallSkill fetches model-supplied URLs with no internal-address restriction
defect.detail: `fetch(source)` follows redirects and accepts any http(s) URL, so the model can probe loopback/link-local endpoints (e.g. cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254) and persist the response body into `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` where it can be read back. Permission gating on the "write" category is the only mitigation.

defect.summary: No Origin validation on the ACP WebSocket upgrade
defect.detail: The upgrade handler checks only the pathname; loopback-only binding is the sole access control. A web page open in the user's browser (or any local process) can connect to ws://127.0.0.1:18889/acp and drive the agent, including tool execution, unless the SDK's `createNodeWebSocketUpgradeHandler` performs its own origin checks. Second-pass 2026-09-30: severity raised medium->high for consistency with the remote-server missing-auth entry: same cross-site WebSocket hijacking profile (browser-initiated local connections are not stopped by loopback binding) driving an agent that executes tools.

defect.summary: Configured paths are interpolated into the seatbelt profile without escaping quotes or parentheses
defect.detail: buildProfile embeds allowWrite/denyWrite paths directly into `(allow file-write* (subpath "${variant}"))` strings. A path containing a double quote (e.g. a workDir or tmpdir with `"` in its name, or an attacker-influenced writable root) can terminate the string literal and inject arbitrary profile rules, potentially granting write access outside the intended sandbox or causing sandbox-exec to fail open/closed unpredictably. The bwrap backend passes paths via argv and is immune; only the seatbelt profile builder performs string interpolation. Review 2026-09-30: originally recorded as a high-severity sandbox escape; reclassified. The interpolation is genuinely unescaped (lines 87, 95-96 after comment cleanup) but not attacker-reachable: allowWrite/denyWrite derive only from host configuration (workDir, "/tmp", tmpdir() at ui/app.tsx:2104, plus the session output dir at tools/bash.ts:239-242), the model cannot influence them, and remote/ACP/print modes never create a sandbox. Triggering requires the user to launch yukino inside a quote-containing directory, and a malformed profile makes sandbox-exec fail closed. Genuine low-severity robustness/defense-in-depth defect, not a practical escape.

defect.summary: Layer 3.5 sandbox auto-allow returns "allow" when Bash args.command is missing or non-string
defect.detail: If strArg(args, "command") yields "" (missing/non-string command), the subcommand list is empty, no deny/ask rule is evaluated, and the checker returns allow with reason "Sandbox auto-allow". This is mitigated in practice because the Bash tool schema requires a string command and Layer 1 evaluates the same empty content, but the layer itself silently approves a call it never actually inspected.

defect.summary: xdotool key names are passed without a `--` end-of-options separator
defect.detail: On Linux, `runXdotool(["key", keys.join("+")])` and the keydown/keyup loops (lines 1107, 1112) pass model-supplied key tokens directly; a token beginning with `-` (e.g. `--sync`, `--clearmodifiers`) would be parsed as an xdotool option rather than a keysym. The `type` action correctly uses `--` (line 1237) but `key`/`keydown`/`keyup` do not. Key names originate from model output, which can be influenced by prompt injection in read content. Uncertain because xdotool may reject or reinterpret such tokens harmlessly in the key subcommand.

defect.summary: Reminder wrapper tags are not escaped against embedded content
defect.detail: addSystemReminder wraps arbitrary content in literal <system-reminder> tags without escaping. Reminder payloads quote externally influenced text (memory files, tool output, teammate mail), so content containing a closing tag can break out of the wrapper and forge reminder-level context for the model.

defect.summary: cancelTmuxSession interpolates a disk-persisted paneId into a double-quoted shell string; a tampered config.json paneId containing ", $() or backticks executes commands in the leader's shell on stop/cancel.
defect.detail: restoreTeammateCancel builds the cancel closure from entry.paneId read out of config.json (backend.ts:80-90, team-file.ts:34, hydrated at index.ts:170); the value flows unvalidated into execSync(`tmux kill-session -t "${sessionName}"`) (backend.ts:68-72). Yukino-generated session names are safe, but the restored value comes from disk with no charset validation — the same double-quote weakness as the recorded new-session injection at backend.ts:107.
